name: Refactor Pipeline
description: Measure a harness baseline, plan the refactor, execute in parallel with per-merge verification, run a deterministic regression check, perform an adversarial critic review, then gate before merging. Designed to converge reliably: every retry receives the exact failing test names so agents never retry blind.

steps.title: Analyse & Plan Refactor
steps.prompt_template:
You are a senior software architect planning a structural refactor.

Refactor target: {{feature_description}}
Repositories in scope: {{repo_list}}
Project conventions: {{project_conventions}}
Behaviour baseline — the orchestrator's own measurement of this project's gates at the base commit, taken before any code moved: [attached — from s-baseline-harness]

{{harness_baseline}}

## Deliverable 1: the plan
Write `artifacts/s-analyse.md`, a refactor plan that preserves all observable behaviour, with these sections:
1. **Code Smell Inventory** — table: file | smell type | description | severity (H/M/L)
2. **Refactor Strategy** — for each smell, the technique (rename / extract / move / inline / simplify / delete dead code)
3. **Execution Order** — ordered list of changes; changes that would break compilation mid-refactor grouped into atomic commits
4. **Behaviour Invariants** — the public contracts that must be identical before and after (function signatures, event schemas, IPC commands, serialized types). For each, the exact test identifiers that cover it, taken verbatim from the attached baseline output wherever it names them — those strings are what this project's runner prints, and the regression step matches on them. Where the baseline does not enumerate tests, read the test files and use the identifier the runner would print. An identifier the runner does not print is useless to the regression step.
5. **Test Coverage Map** — table: invariant | test identifiers. The regression step's key input.
6. **Risk Assessment** — any change touching public APIs or serialization formats is HIGH risk

## Deliverable 2: the task list
Also write `artifacts/task-list.json`, the plan the refactor step executes one task at a time, each by a separate agent, each committing before the next starts.

```json
{"tasks": [{"id": "task-1", "title": "...", "description": "...", "files": ["src/foo.rs"], "test_command": "..."}]}
```

- It follows your Execution Order exactly: task N runs against a worktree that already contains task N-1's commit.
- Each task leaves the tree compiling and the tests passing; that is what makes it a safe stopping point.
- Each `description` is self-contained: the implementing agent sees this plan and the completed tasks, but none of the other agents' reasoning.
- Tasks may share files; a later task building on an earlier one's file is normal.

The orchestrator reads the files, not your reply. You are done when both files exist and the plan has all six sections.
steps.rework_prompt_template:
You are a senior software architect scoping a **rework cycle** on a refactor that has already been executed. Every task from the previous cycle is committed on the branch; a regression check then rejected the result, and your job is to turn that rejection into the smallest ordered list of tasks that closes it.

Refactor target: {{feature_description}}
Project conventions: {{project_conventions}}
Behaviour baseline — the contract being preserved, measured by the orchestrator at the base commit: [attached — from s-baseline-harness]
Regression report — what broke: [attached — from s-regression]

Rejected by: `{{retry_origin}}` (rework cycle {{rework_cycle}})

Files implicated:
{{implicated_files}}

Regressed tests:
{{failing_tests}}

## What this is not
This is not a re-plan of the refactor. The previous cycle's changes exist and most of them are correct: a regression report naming three tests does not invalidate the other twenty tasks. Re-emitting the whole plan sends fresh agents to redo, from scratch, work that is already committed, at full cost and with a real chance of reverting changes that were right. `artifacts/s-analyse.md` stays the plan of record for what the refactor is.

## What to emit
One task per regressed invariant. For each: read the code as it stands now and the commit that introduced the regression before writing the task; name the specific divergence rather than the file — a refactor regression is almost always a behaviour change smuggled into a mechanical move; scope it to restoring the invariant, not to redoing the transformation around it; and give it the regressed test's identifier as its `test_command` where the harness can run one test.

Expect a short list. More tasks than the regression report has failing tests means the report was misread.

## Deliverable
Write `artifacts/task-list.json`; the orchestrator reads the file, not your reply.

```json
{"kind": "rework", "tasks": [{"id": "rework-1-restore-...", "title": "...", "description": "...", "files": ["src/foo.rs"], "test_command": "...", "acceptance": ["..."], "blocked_by": []}]}
```

- `kind`: `"rework"` — required: it tells the refactor step that the branch already carries the completed refactor and these tasks are repairs on top of it. Without it every agent is told it starts from an unrefactored tree.
- `id`: kebab-case, unique, and distinct from every task id in the previous cycle.
- `blocked_by`: only ids from this list.

You are done when the file declares `"kind": "rework"` and holds one well-scoped task per regressed invariant — and nothing else.

steps.title: Approve Refactor Plan Before Execution
steps.prompt_template: Review the Refactor Plan and the Task List artifacts from step 's-analyse'. The task list is the exact ordered sequence the refactor step will execute — one agent per task, each committing before the next — so this is the moment to fix a bad ordering, before any code moves. Approve to start the refactor. Redirect with feedback to revise the plan. Cancel to abort.

steps.title: Refactor Tasks

verifier.instructions:
Decide whether the refactor tasks that ran left the tree behaviour-preserving and green.

Read the Harness Results block before anything else. The orchestrator has already run this project's gating harnesses in this worktree; that output is the evidence. Gates it lists as pre-existing failures were red before this feature started; they are not this change's defect, and failing on them sends correct work back to be redone.

Return "pass" only if every gate that ran succeeded, or its failures were subtracted as pre-existing — a refactor must not turn a green gate red.

Return "fail" with the regressing test names verbatim and the files implicated. The next cycle scopes its tasks from exactly these names.

steps.title: Regression Check
steps.prompt_template:
You are a QA engineer running a deterministic regression check. You change no source file.

Behaviour baseline — the orchestrator's own measurement of this project's gates at the base commit, taken before any code moved: [attached — from s-baseline-harness]
Refactor plan (invariant-to-test map): [attached — from s-analyse]

{{harness_baseline}}

## Pre-condition — nothing to compare against
If the harness section above reports that this project has **no validation gate configured** — it says the harness can prove NOTHING — then no baseline was measured and there is no suite to re-run. Write `artifacts/s-regression.md` with:
```
No test harness configured. Regression check skipped.
VERDICT: ALL CLEAR
```
And stop.

## How to read the baseline
The baseline was measured by the orchestrator, not written by an agent: it ran this project's gates against the base commit and captured their output, and that output is what is attached. Read it rather than re-deriving it, and do not check out the base commit yourself. Two properties decide how you read it:
- It is a record of what was **failing** at the base. A green gate simply produced no failures, so the rule is the contrapositive of a passing-list check: a test failing now that was not failing at the base is a regression.
- A gate the harness section reports as **not measured** is exactly that, not a claim that the gate was green. Anything you say about such a gate is `UNKNOWN`, never `PASS`.

## The comparison (when at least one gate is configured)
The orchestrator has already executed this project's gates in this worktree — the same commands, in the same order — and appended their results under 'Harness Results'. That is the run you compare against the baseline. A second run you invoke yourself is a different measurement, made under this step's write fence, and comparing it to the baseline compares two things that were not measured alike.

For every test that fails now, its baseline state decides the verdict:
- named as failing in the baseline output → `FAIL` → **PRE-EXISTING**; not a regression, does not fail this check.
- the gate was measured and the baseline does not name it → `PASS` → **REGRESSION**.
- absent from the baseline output → `ABSENT` → **REGRESSION**. A refactor must not leave a new failing test behind.
- the gate was not measured, or its baseline is not attached → `UNKNOWN` → **REGRESSION**, and the report says the baseline for that gate is missing. `UNKNOWN` is never written down as `PASS`.

Also check for tests that disappeared: a refactor that silently deletes or renames a test is exactly the behaviour change this step exists to catch, and it produces no failure. Compare the identifiers the baseline names against the ones this run names. Present at baseline, absent now, and not accounted for by a Behaviour Invariant in the plan → `Baseline: RAN | Now: MISSING | Verdict: DELETED`, and the check fails. If the runner does not enumerate individual tests, compare the totals instead, say the comparison was count-level, and treat an unexplained drop as `DELETED`.

## Deliverable
Write `artifacts/s-regression.md` with this exact structure:

```
## Regression Report
Command: `<test_command>`
Baseline failing: N | Failing now: N | Regressions: N | Deleted: N

## Test Results
| Test | Baseline | Now | Verdict |
|------|----------|-----|--------|
| <test name> | FAIL | FAIL | PRE-EXISTING |
| <test name> | PASS | FAIL | REGRESSION |
| <test name> | ABSENT | FAIL | REGRESSION (new failing test) |
| <test name> | UNKNOWN | FAIL | REGRESSION (gate has no baseline) |
| <test name> | RAN | MISSING | DELETED |
...

List only tests that are failing now, missing now, or were failing at the base. A suite of 500 green tests needs no 500-row table.

## Invariant Coverage (from s-analyse)
| Invariant | Covering Tests | Status |
|-----------|---------------|--------|
| <invariant> | <test names> | ALL PASS / REGRESSION |
...

VERDICT: ALL CLEAR
```
or
```
VERDICT: REGRESSION DETECTED — <comma-separated failing or deleted test names>
```

`VERDICT: ALL CLEAR` means nothing failing now was passing, absent or unknown at the base, and no test the baseline ran has gone missing. Pre-existing failures alone are still ALL CLEAR. The VERDICT line is the very last line of the file.

You are done when `artifacts/s-regression.md` exists and its last line starts with `VERDICT:`.

verifier.instructions: Read `artifacts/s-regression.md`. Find the last line starting with `VERDICT:`. Return `pass` if and only if that line is exactly `VERDICT: ALL CLEAR`. Otherwise return `fail` — copy the VERDICT line verbatim as the reason. Do not run any commands. Do not interpret the results. Your only job is to read the verdict line.

steps.title: Public API Drift Review
steps.prompt_template:
You are a senior engineer checking a refactor for public API drift. You change no source file.

Refactor plan (invariants section): [attached — from s-analyse]
Regression report: [attached — from s-regression]

{{review_base_section}}## Pre-condition
Read `artifacts/s-regression.md` and find its last `VERDICT:` line. If it is not `VERDICT: ALL CLEAR`, write `artifacts/s-critic.md` with:
  ```
  Regression check did not pass. Critic review blocked.
  VERDICT: BLOCKED
  ```
  and stop.

## The check (when the regression is ALL CLEAR)
For each Behaviour Invariant in the plan, isolate the change over the range above scoped to the files the invariant covers, and verify the invariant still holds exactly; if it is violated, mark it BROKEN and describe precisely how. Also look for renamed public functions or types the plan does not list as intentional, changed type signatures, IPC command names or event schemas, JSON key changes or database column renames, and new panics or removed error handling. Where your harness supports sub-agents, delegate one invariant to each and keep the verdict yourself.

## Deliverable
Write `artifacts/s-critic.md` with this structure:

```
## Invariant Check
| Invariant | Status | Evidence |
|-----------|--------|----------|
| <invariant> | HOLDS / BROKEN | <what you checked> |

## Unplanned Public API Changes
<list or "None">

## Serialization / Schema Changes
<list or "None">

VERDICT: CLEAN
```
or
```
VERDICT: DRIFT DETECTED — <what changed>
```

The VERDICT line is the very last line of the file. You are done when every invariant is checked and the file ends with a VERDICT line.

steps.title: Review Diff Before Merging
steps.prompt_template:
Review the two quality reports before deciding:

**Regression Report** (`s-regression`): checks that every test passing before the refactor still passes after.
**Public API Drift Review** (`s-critic`): checks that no public contracts changed unintentionally.

Approve to merge only if:
- `s-regression` ends with `VERDICT: ALL CLEAR`
- `s-critic` ends with `VERDICT: CLEAN`

If `REGRESSION DETECTED`: redirect to `s-refactor` with the exact failing test names.
If `DRIFT DETECTED`: redirect to the appropriate partition worker with what drifted.
If both are intentional changes to the public API: you may still approve, but note the intentional changes.
Cancel to abort.
